title: SPA/514/2013 of Uttarakhand Public Service Commission AND ANOTHER Vs Himanshu Nautiyal AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
 Special Appeal No. 514 of 2013
Uttarakhand Public Service Commission
And others
 ÖÖÖÖÖAppellants
Versus
1. Himanshu Nautiyal S/o Sri Shailendra Kumar Nautiyal
2. State of Uttarakhand
 ÖÖÖÖÖ.Respondents
Mr. B.D. Kandpal, Advocate, present for the appellants.
Mr. Pankaj Miglani, Advocate for respondent no. 1.
Ms. Puja Banga, Brief Holder for the State/respondent no. 2.
Honíble V.K. Bist, ACJ.
Honíble U.C. Dhyani, J
Learned counsel for the private respondents submits
that he is not opposing the delay condonation application. In
view of this statement and in view of the facts mentioned in
the affidavit, delay condonation application is allowed and
delay of 72 days in filing the special appeal is condoned.
Present special appeal is being preferred against the
judgment and order dated 06.09.2013, passed in writ
petition no. 650 of 2013 (S/S).
Controversy before us is whether the rejection of the
candidature of the petitioner on the ground that his name is
not registered with the Employment Exchange in State of
Uttarakhand is correct or not? Learned Single Judge, by
relying on the judgment passed by the Court in the matter
of Ashwani Rawat Vs. Uttarakhand Public Service
Commission and other [Writ Petition No. 477 of 2013 (S/S)]

2
dated 6
th September 2013, reached to the conclusion that the
employees of Uttarakhand Jal Vidyut Nigam Ltd./ Jal
Sansthan, which is an instrumentality of the State, will also
be covered by the exemption clause in favour of the
Government employee from registration in the employment
exchange. Learned Single Judge allowed the writ petition.
It is contended by the learned counsel for the private
respondent that Judgment of Ashwani Rawat (supra) was
challenged by the Uttarakhand Public Service Commission
in Special Appeal No. 430 of 2013 and the Division Bench
upheld the judgment and dismissed the special appeal.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that against said
judgment, SLP was filed in the Honíble Supreme Court
which is still pending. In said appeal, Honíble Supreme
Court has stayed the contempt proceedings.
We have considered the judgment passed by learned
Single Judge and also judgment passed by the Division
Bench in Special Appeal No. 430 of 2013. In our view, the
controversy involved in the present appeal is squarely
covered by the judgment given in Special Appeal No. 430 of
2013.
We accordingly dismiss the special appeal.
In the end, learned counsel for the appellants submits
that the contempt proceedings are pending before the
learned Single Judge in which 23rd January 2015 is fixed. He
prayed that direction be issued for the deferment of the
contempt proceedings. At this, learned counsel for the
private respondent submits that he will not press the

3
contempt petition on 23rd January 2015. We donít think any
order is required to be passed in this regard in view of the
aforesaid statement of learned counsel for the private
respondent.
All the pending applications also stand disposed of.
 (U.C. Dhyani, J.) (V.K. Bist, ACJ.)
20.01.2015
Parul
